---
description: "How NCodeGroup services handle async code, cancellation, background work and concurrency across replicas: atomic claims and takes, single-flight refresh, hosted-service lifecycles, job dispatch, broadcasts and shared retrievals."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.ts, **/*.tsx, **/charts/**, build/**/*.ps1"
---

# Async and concurrency

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Use single-use shared state (login transactions, `state` values, authorization codes, one-time codes, replay nonces) through one atomic operation on a store that every replica shares: an atomic take such as `GETDEL` to redeem it, and an atomic add-if-absent such as `SET NX` or `TryAdd` to record a replay. Never read and then remove or write in two steps, and never keep this state per replica.** A check followed by a separate write lets two concurrent or replayed presentations both succeed, on the same replica or on different ones. *Check:* Look for `GetAsync`/`Contains` followed by `RemoveAsync`/`SetAsync` on single-use or replay state, single-use records that are never deleted, and one-time state held in in-memory or per-replica structures. <sub>Identity ADR-0164; Identity ADR-0267; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Update shared state that concurrent requests may change with a compare-and-swap that names the version you read. When the swap fails, reload and retry or fail; never fall back to an unconditional overwrite.** Blind overwrites lose concurrent updates, such as tokens that another replica has just rotated. *Check:* Look for a read-modify-write on shared or distributed state that ends in an unconditional `Set`/`Replace`, ignores the result of a conditional replace, or overwrites after a failed replace. *Note:* The csharp-production instructions also say to encrypt stored values that hold secrets and to fail closed when the store fails. <sub>Identity ADR-0267; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When a request and a background pass, or several requests, can end or process the same record, run the once-only follow-up effects (logout notifications, cascading revocation, audit or log events) only when an atomic claim (a revoke-once, conditional update or affected-row check) reports that this call made the transition. A claim must return false when the item was already in the target state, was unknown, or lost a race.** Without a claim, both paths act on the item, so relying parties are notified twice and the event is audited twice. *Check:* Look for code that reads state and then dispatches a command, notification or audit event without branching on the result of an atomic claim, code that dispatches when the claim returned false, and claim methods that return true for items that were already ended. <sub>Identity ADR-0098; Identity ADR-0220; Identity ADR-0223; Identity ADR-0227; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Take the data that a follow-up action needs from the state that the claim, compare-and-swap or conditional update itself read and returned, not from an earlier separate read.** An earlier read can be stale. For example, a client added to a session between the read and the claim would not be notified. *Check:* Look for code that reads an entity, claims or conditionally updates it, and then acts on fields from the first read. Also look for claim APIs that return only a bool when callers need the claimed state. <sub>Identity ADR-0228; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Present a rotating refresh token at most once across the cluster. Serialize refreshes of a session locally, and admit one refresher across replicas through a lease keyed by the session key plus a SHA-256 fingerprint of the refresh token, not by a record version. A caller that loses the lease polls with backoff for the winner's result and fails with 503 at the lease duration. It never retries with the refresh token it read earlier.** Presenting a rotated refresh token twice counts as reuse, and the provider revokes the whole token family (RFC 9700 §4.14.2). A lease keyed by version is unsafe because unrelated writes change the version. *Check:* Look for refresh logic that has only an in-process lock or no coordination, a lease keyed by version or timestamp, or a timeout or store-error path that calls the token endpoint outside the lease or resends the old refresh token. <sub>Identity ADR-0291; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Pass `CancellationToken.None` to work that must finish once a change is committed or a point of no return is passed. This covers security effects after a commit (ending sessions or revoking tokens after a password change, disable or block), recording failed authentication attempts, removing the local session record and its cookie on logout (before any remote revocation call), and a non-idempotent remote operation run under a won lease, such as a refresh-token rotation, together with its write-back. Bound that work by its own timeout. Steps that run before the commit keep the request token.** A client that disconnects must not leave a committed change without its security effect, skip a failed-attempt count, leave its session behind, or lose a rotated token so that the next refresh counts as reuse. *Check:* Look for `HttpContext.RequestAborted` or the caller's token passed to post-commit follow-ups, failed-attempt recording, session removal, or token requests and write-backs inside a lease. Also look for pre-commit steps that pass `CancellationToken.None`, and for logout that removes the session only after remote calls. Expect a test that cancels partway through. <sub>Identity ADR-0226; Identity ADR-0237; Identity ADR-0291; Identity ADR-0293; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Enforce a limit or keep a count that all replicas must agree on with an atomic increment on a shared expiring counter store. Increment before judging the request, and count what was requested rather than what later succeeded. Do not use in-process `System.Threading.RateLimiting` limiters or `AddRateLimiter` for limits that must hold across replicas.** A read followed by a later write loses concurrent increments. An in-process limiter admits N times its limit on N replicas. *Check:* Look for counters that are read, incremented in memory and written back, counters incremented only on success, and `FixedWindowRateLimiter`/`SlidingWindowRateLimiter`/`TokenBucketRateLimiter` used for tenant or client limits in a multi-replica service. <sub>Identity ADR-0196; Identity ADR-0198; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Don't let correctness depend on process-local state. State that must outlive a request or be visible to another replica belongs in the database or a shared-state store. In-memory caches hold only data that can be rebuilt on a miss. Never write durable data to the local filesystem.** Replicas are interchangeable and disposable, and any one of them may serve the next request. *Check:* Look for static or singleton fields, or `IMemoryCache` entries, that hold authoritative state, and for file writes of durable data. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In a background loop, treat an `OperationCanceledException` as shutdown only when the loop's own stopping token is cancelled. Catch a failed unit of work with `when (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)` and handle any other cancellation, such as an `HttpClient` timeout, as an ordinary failure.** A timeout throws `TaskCanceledException` while the stopping token is untouched. A loop that exits on every cancellation ends there, and under `BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost` the whole host stops. *Check:* Look for `catch (OperationCanceledException)`/`catch (TaskCanceledException)` that breaks or returns without checking the stopping token, and for filters such as `exception is not OperationCanceledException`. <sub>Identity ADR-0232; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When a timeout is enforced with a `CancellationTokenSource` linked to the caller's token, for example on outbound fetches of untrusted URLs (which must always have a configurable timeout), convert only the timeout's cancellation into a domain or validation error. Let the caller's own cancellation propagate unchanged.** Without a timeout, a slow remote host ties up the server. Converting every cancellation hides real caller cancellation as a fetch failure. *Check:* Look for untrusted outbound fetches with no timeout or with a timeout not linked to the caller's token, and for `catch (OperationCanceledException)` that converts every cancellation without checking whether the caller's token requested it. <sub>Identity ADR-0095; Identity ADR-0111</sub>
- **Work deferred past the request (background handlers, event and audit sinks) must use a snapshot of the request context (correlation or trace id, request id, tenant, actor, client, source IP) taken when the work is enqueued or the event is published. It must run in a fresh `IServiceScopeFactory` scope and use an application-lifetime token, never the request token.** By the time background work runs, `HttpContext`, the request scope and `Activity.Current` are gone, and the request token is already cancelled. *Check:* Look for background handlers or sinks that read `HttpContext`, `IHttpContextAccessor` or `Activity.Current`, resolve services from the request scope, or receive the request `CancellationToken`. <sub>Identity ADR-0047; Identity ADR-0283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Run an outbound side effect that must happen after a request returns (webhooks, client notifications, back-channel logout, audit delivery) by dispatching a job through a job-dispatch abstraction. Do not make an inline, single-attempt HTTP call whose failure is logged and dropped.** Inline best-effort delivery cannot be retried, and it fixes the delivery strategy in place, so a deployment cannot make delivery durable. *Check:* Look for request-handling code that POSTs to a relying party or external endpoint inline after a state change, catches and logs the failure, and does not retry. <sub>Identity ADR-0074; Identity ADR-0090</sub>
- **Make background job handlers idempotent, keyed on the stable dispatch id, and make every handler registered as a singleton thread-safe.** Dispatch is at-least-once: a retry or a durable adapter can run a job again, and several consumers can run a singleton handler at the same time. *Check:* Look for handlers whose side effects (issuing, sending, writing) would duplicate harmfully on redelivery, handlers that ignore the dispatch id, and singleton handlers with unsynchronized mutable state. <sub>Identity ADR-0090; Identity ADR-0232</sub>
- **Define a dispatched job type as a plain, serializable data object with no behaviour, captured delegates or service references. Behaviour belongs in a separate handler keyed by the job type.** Durable or distributed adapters (outbox, broker, scheduler) have to persist and rebuild the job, and a delegate or a live object can't be serialized. *Check:* Look for job or work-item types with `Func`/`Action` fields, lambdas, service instances, or `HttpContext`/`DbContext`/stream state. <sub>Identity ADR-0090</sub>
- **Bound every background queue and give it an explicit policy for when it is full. Best-effort items may be dropped, but every drop must be counted or logged. Compliance-grade audit records must never be dropped; they block or spill to durable storage.** Back-pressure has to be a deliberate decision, and compliance audit needs at-least-once delivery. *Check:* Look for unbounded channels or queues, drops that are neither logged nor counted, and audit paths that drop records when the queue is full. <sub>Identity ADR-0047</sub>
- **Honor the host's stopping token so in-flight work drains and the process stops gracefully. Do not use in-process queues or fire-and-forget tasks for work that must survive a replica being replaced. Run long full-scan passes in their own hosted service, not on a shared in-process job dispatcher.** In-process dispatch loses queued jobs when a replica is replaced, and a long pass holds a dispatcher worker ahead of time-sensitive deliveries. *Check:* Look for background services that ignore `stoppingToken`, fire-and-forget tasks or in-memory queues used for work that must not be lost, and walks over all tenants or entities queued on a shared dispatcher. <sub>Identity ADR-0134; Identity ADR-0219</sub>
- **Make a hosted service's `StopAsync` run its final work (flush or cleanup) exactly once. Start it under a `Lock`, memoize the task, and return that same task to every concurrent or later caller. Serialize it with the periodic work through a semaphore, never throw, and log what could not be finished. A service that buffers data in memory must flush it one last time on a graceful stop.** A host can be stopped twice at once. The stop that returns first lets its caller dispose services, including logging, while the other stop is still running. Overlapping periodic and final flushes can apply or drop the same data twice or out of order. *Check:* Look for `StopAsync` overrides that start a flush on every call, return early on a second call without awaiting the work in progress, can throw, or share a queue with a periodic flush without synchronization. Also look for buffering services that never flush on stop, and shared counters updated without `Interlocked`. <sub>Identity ADR-0199; Identity ADR-0209; Identity ADR-0303; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Run periodic background work as a hosted service that ticks a `PeriodicTimer` driven by the injected `TimeProvider`. Inside the loop, catch a failed pass, log it as a warning with a defined event id, and run again at the next tick. Never let an exception, including cancellation on stop, escape `ExecuteAsync`.** A transient failure must not stop the maintenance permanently or crash the host, and the service must shut down cleanly. *Check:* Look for loops using `Task.Delay` or `System.Threading.Timer` without `TimeProvider`, exceptions escaping `ExecuteAsync`, and failures swallowed without logging. <sub>Identity ADR-0218; Identity ADR-0223</sub>
- **When several replicas run the same periodic pass, have each one take a lease for the current window: atomically add an expiring key derived from the window (UTC ticks divided by interval ticks) that expires when the window ends, and skip the pass if the add fails. The work itself must still be safe to run twice.** Without a lease, every replica scans and claims the same items. The once-only claims keep an accidental double run harmless. *Check:* Look for new periodic jobs in multi-replica services with no shared per-interval lease, and lease keys that do not expire with the window. <sub>Identity ADR-0223</sub>
- **Release an expiring distributed lease only when the work finished with a safety margin before the lease expires, and only if you still own it.** Releasing after expiry can delete a lease that another replica has since taken, which admits a second concurrent holder. *Check:* Look for unconditional lease or lock release in `finally` blocks that does not check ownership or the remaining lease time. <sub>Identity ADR-0291</sub>
- **Key a lease or 'already processed' marker for work triggered by a state change on both the row's concurrency token and the state fingerprint.** A fingerprint alone skips a return to an earlier state, even though entities created in between were reconciled only against the other state. *Check:* Look for dedup or lease keys built only from a content hash or state value, with no version or concurrency token. <sub>Identity ADR-0219</sub>
- **Do not hold a striped lock across a long or unbounded wait (remote leases, polling, I/O). Use per-key locks that are reference-counted and removed when the last waiter leaves.** While a stripe is held, unrelated keys that hash to it block and time out. *Check:* Look for striped `SemaphoreSlim` or lock arrays held across polling loops or remote waits, and per-key lock dictionaries that never remove entries. <sub>Identity ADR-0291; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **When concurrent callers need the same expensive remote resource, share one in-flight retrieval: a `ConcurrentDictionary` of `Lazy<Task<T>>` keyed by the resource, with the entry removed when the retrieval ends. Run the retrieval with `CancellationToken.None`, bounded by its own timeout, and have each caller await it with `WaitAsync(cancellationToken)`. Give it its own copies of disposable inputs (for example, a fresh `X509Certificate2` loaded from the raw data), and remember a failure for a configured time.** Otherwise a burst of requests repeats the download, one caller's cancellation or disposal breaks the retrieval for everyone else, and an unreachable source costs every request a timeout. *Check:* Look for cache-miss paths where each concurrent miss starts its own fetch, shared tasks started with the first caller's token or awaited without `WaitAsync`, shared tasks that capture caller-owned `IDisposable`s, and failing sources retried on every request. <sub>Identity ADR-0252; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Publish a lazily created shared client with `Volatile.Read` and `Interlocked.CompareExchange`, and don't cache a failed creation, so the next call tries again.** A transient failure during creation must not break the component permanently. *Check:* Look for `Lazy<T>` or cached `Task` fields that keep a faulted creation, and for unsynchronized lazy initialization of shared clients. <sub>Identity ADR-0260</sub>
- **In a concurrent cache, publish related data as one atomic entry, or publish the primary item only after the data it depends on is stored.** A concurrent reader can otherwise see the item without its dependents, for example a certificate without its issuer chain, and build and cache a broken result. *Check:* Look for writes to separate dictionaries where the primary entry is added before the data that depends on it. <sub>Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Announce a change that other replicas must see through a replica broadcast. Apply the change locally first and publish afterwards. Once the write has committed, log a failed publish rather than throwing.** In-process caches on other replicas go stale otherwise, and a failed publish must not fail a write that has already committed. *Check:* Look for caches invalidated only locally, a publish that happens before the local apply, or a publish failure that is thrown after the commit. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make broadcast and pub/sub handlers idempotent and independent of ordering. Whenever a subscription is first established or restored after a reconnect, assume messages were missed and evict or re-read everything they could have invalidated.** Delivery is best effort, at most once and unordered; the publisher's own replica also receives its message; and messages sent while a replica was disconnected never arrive. *Check:* Look for handlers that assume a single, ordered delivery or do non-idempotent work (increments, appends, one-time effects), and subscribers with no invalidate-all path on subscribe or connection restore. <sub>Identity ADR-0205; Identity ADR-0219; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Hand each incoming pub/sub message to its handlers on a thread-pool thread, not inline on the connection's receive callback.** A slow handler must not stop the connection from receiving other messages. *Check:* Look for subscription callbacks that run or await handler work synchronously inside the receive callback. <sub>Identity ADR-0205</sub>
- **Process a queue of independent jobs with a bounded number of concurrent consumers, for example several loops reading one `Channel` created with `SingleReader = false`. Don't use a single serial loop or `Parallel.ForEachAsync`.** In a single loop, one slow endpoint holds up every job. In `Parallel.ForEachAsync`, one exception cancels every running job. *Check:* Look for dispatch workers with a single reader loop, `Parallel.ForEachAsync` over a channel, or several consumers reading a channel created with `SingleReader = true`. <sub>Identity ADR-0232</sub>
- **When a batched delete in a multi-replica cleanup loop fails with a concurrency exception because another replica deleted the same rows, treat it as progress and continue with the next batch.** Losing that race means the work is being done elsewhere; concurrent pruners waste at most one batch. *Check:* Look for cleanup loops that abort or log an error on a store concurrency exception during save, instead of reading the next batch. <sub>Identity ADR-0213</sub>
- **When an authorization server's refresh-token rotation loses a concurrency race to another rotation of the same token and a reuse interval is configured, re-read the grant and answer as a retry instead of treating it as reuse.** Two tabs that refresh at the same time must both keep their session instead of tripping reuse detection. *Check:* Look for rotation code that treats any concurrency conflict as reuse and revokes the lineage without re-reading the grant. <sub>Identity ADR-0217</sub>
- **Before a background service reads the store or depends on server state, have it await a readiness signal that the server has been built.** A pass must not run against the store before the server is ready. *Check:* Look for hosted services that query persistence at the start of `ExecuteAsync`/`StartAsync` without first awaiting a readiness signal. <sub>Identity ADR-0223</sub>
- **Keep ambient context that must reach data contexts created by `IDbContextFactory` from the root provider, such as the current tenant, in an `AsyncLocal<T>`, not in a scoped service or an `HttpContext` item.** Factory-created contexts live outside the request's DI scope, so a scoped holder would leave them without a tenant. *Check:* Look for ambient tenant accessors that keep the current value in a scoped-service field or in `HttpContext.Items`. <sub>Identity ADR-0018</sub>
- **Do the asynchronous step of loading or unwrapping key material, which may call a remote KMS, once through an async acquisition method, and keep the resulting protector's cryptography synchronous. When caching unwrapped keys, don't store a load that an eviction overtook, and don't zero key memory on eviction; zero it only when the owning cache is disposed.** Only loading master keys should reach the KMS. A protector handed out earlier may still be using an evicted key, and caching a load that raced an eviction brings back stale keys. *Check:* Look for async encrypt/decrypt methods or KMS calls on the hot path, sync-over-async KMS calls, eviction code that clears key buffers, and load-then-store code that doesn't check for an eviction during the load. <sub>Identity ADR-0235</sub>
- **In a React effect that runs an async load, list the loader as a dependency, abort the in-flight load in the cleanup, and ignore any result or error that settles after it is no longer the current load. Tie error state to the loader that produced it, so that replacing the loader clears the error.** Only the current load may report state. A late result, or a StrictMode remount, must not overwrite newer state or leave a stale error visible. *Check:* Look for async effects that leave the loader out of the dependencies, have no `AbortController` or cleanup, or call `setState`/`dispatch` without checking that the load is still current. Also look for error state that persists after the loader changes. <sub>Identity ADR-0156</sub>
- **Use `Task.Run` for fire-and-forget offloading, and only when the work really must leave the calling thread. Never use `Task.Factory.StartNew` with an async delegate.** `StartNew` with an async lambda returns an unobserved `Task<Task>` and drops the inner task's exceptions. *Check:* Look for `Task.Factory.StartNew` with an async lambda, and for offloading that isn't needed. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make async methods return `ValueTask`/`ValueTask<T>`, end their names in `Async`, and take a `CancellationToken` as the last parameter. Return `Task` only where a framework contract you don't own requires it (middleware `InvokeAsync`, minimal-API handlers, mediator handlers). Don't add `ConfigureAwait(false)` in server-side code.** This is the house async shape. Server hosts have no `SynchronizationContext`, so `ConfigureAwait(false)` only adds noise. *Check:* Look for new async methods returning `Task` outside framework boundaries, missing `Async` suffixes, a `CancellationToken` that isn't the last parameter, and added `.ConfigureAwait(false)`. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0285</sub>
- **In Helm charts for replicas that keep single-use state in-process with no shared store, use the `Recreate` deployment strategy and refuse more than one replica. Use `RollingUpdate` with `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0` only when that state is shared.** A rolling update, even with `maxSurge: 0`, can start the new pod while the old one is still serving, so their separate single-use state overlaps. *Check:* Look for `RollingUpdate` (including `maxSurge: 0`), or allowing `replicas > 1`, when no shared state store is configured. <sub>Identity ADR-0179</sub>
- **When Aspire runs JavaScript resources from a shared pnpm workspace, call `WithPnpm(install: false)` and install the workspace once, serially, from a single bootstrap script. Never add a per-app `pnpm install`.** Concurrent `pnpm install` runs against the shared, symlinked `node_modules` collide with `ERR_PNPM_EBUSY` and fail the dependent resource. *Check:* Look for `WithPnpm()` without `install: false`, and for per-app `pnpm install` steps in orchestration or repair scripts. <sub>Identity ADR-0071</sub>
